questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis with clean base and bilateral non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. Which is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose — the WHO and CDC first-line recommendation.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset of painful erythematous nodules on the face and extremities with fever and joint pains. Nerve function is intact. Which type of lepra reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2) is an immune complex-mediated reaction seen in BL/LL leprosy, presenting with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic symptoms. Nerve function is usually intact initially.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal skin and mucous membranes, with positive Nikolsky sign. Histology shows subepidermal blister with eosinophils. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae on normal or erythematous skin. Histology shows subepidermal blister with eosinophils. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at BMZ. Anti-BP180 and anti-BP230 antibodies are characteristic.

questions.q: A 42-year-old farmer presents with verrucous plaques on the foot with black dots. KOH mount shows 'copper penny' or 'medlar bodies' (sclerotic cells). Which organism is most commonly responsible?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is most commonly caused by Fonsecaea pedrosoi. The pathognomonic finding is muriform/sclerotic cells (Medlar bodies or copper penny bodies) seen on histology or KOH mount.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted erosions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or rarely Streptococcus). Topical mupirocin 2% is the first-line treatment for localized disease as it is bactericidal and has low resistance rates.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the genitalia with painful inguinal lymphadenopathy. This is his second episode. The drug used for suppressive therapy is:
questions.exp: Genital herpes suppressive therapy with acyclovir 400 mg BD (or valacyclovir 500 mg OD) significantly reduces recurrences and transmission. Acyclovir 400 mg BD is the standard suppressive regimen.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with pruritic papules and vesicles in a herpetiform pattern over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows subepidermal blister with neutrophils at dermal papillary tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is characterized by intensely pruritic vesicles over extensor surfaces, granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae on DIF, and association with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Treatment: dapsone and gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 55-year-old female on long-term hydroxychloroquine for SLE presents with photosensitivity, discoid rashes, and oral ulcers. Lab shows anti-dsDNA positive, ANA 1:640 speckled pattern. Which finding is most specific for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are highly specific for SLE (95% specificity) and correlate with disease activity and lupus nephritis. ANA is sensitive but not specific. Anti-Ro is seen in subacute cutaneous LE and neonatal LE. Anti-histone is characteristic of drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas destroying neurovascular bundles in the dermis. Ridley-Jopling classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid (TT) leprosy: few well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic lesions, negative smear (paucibacillary), epithelioid granulomas with giant cells destroying dermal nerves on histology. High cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: A patient with psoriasis has silvery scales on an erythematous base. Removal of scales reveals pinpoint bleeding. This sign is called:
questions.exp: Auspitz sign: pinpoint bleeding seen on removal of psoriatic scales due to thinned suprapapillary epidermis over dilated tortuous capillaries in elongated dermal papillae. It is characteristic of psoriasis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with periorbital heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules over knuckles, and proximal muscle weakness. Which autoantibody is associated with interstitial lung disease in this condition?
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis with anti-Jo-1 antibody (antisynthetase syndrome) is associated with interstitial lung disease, mechanic's hands, and Raynaud's phenomenon. Anti-Mi-2 is associated with classic DM with good prognosis. Anti-TIF1-gamma is associated with malignancy-associated DM.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with a single painless genital ulcer followed by painful, fluctuant unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain of pus shows 'school of fish' pattern. Causative organism?
questions.exp: Chancroid (caused by Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with painful genital ulcer and painful bubo. Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern. Treatment: azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250mg IM.

questions.q: A patient presents with excessive scaling of the scalp, face, and trunk following a febrile illness. Histology of an elliptical biopsy shows parakeratosis with neutrophils in stratum corneum (Munro microabscesses). Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum) and spongiform pustules of Kogoj are hallmarks of psoriasis histology. These combined with parakeratosis, acanthosis, and elongated rete ridges are diagnostic.

questions.q: A 12-year-old girl presents with scaly patches on the scalp with broken hair shafts. Wood's lamp shows bright green fluorescence. KOH mount shows ectothrix pattern. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes tinea capitis with ectothrix infection (spores outside hair shaft) and bright green fluorescence on Wood's lamp. Trichophyton species cause endothrix infections and do not fluoresce. Treatment: oral griseofulvin or terbinafine.

questions.q: A 70-year-old male presents with a pearly translucent nodule with rolled telangiectatic borders and central ulceration on the nose. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Noduloulcerative (rodent ulcer) basal cell carcinoma presents as a pearly nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasia, and central ulceration typically on sun-exposed areas of the face (nose is most common site). It is the most common skin cancer.

questions.q: A 32-year-old male with HIV presents with multiple violaceous papules and plaques on the skin, oral cavity, and GIT. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated red blood cells. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma (AIDS-associated/epidemic type) presents with violaceous lesions in HIV patients with CD4 <200. Caused by HHV-8. Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and plasma cells. Treatment: HAART; advanced disease: liposomal doxorubicin.

questions.q: A patient with severe atopic dermatitis is started on dupilumab. What is the mechanism of action?
opts: Anti-IL-4 receptor alpha subunit monoclonal antibody blocking IL-4 and IL-13 signaling
questions.exp: Dupilumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-4 receptor alpha subunit, blocking both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling — the key Th2 cytokines in atopic dermatitis pathogenesis. It is FDA/EMA approved for moderate-to-severe AD.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with a firm, skin-coloured nodule on the shin that dimples inward on lateral compression (Fitzpatrick sign). Histology shows spindle cells in a storiform pattern with hemosiderin deposits. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatofibroma (benign fibrous histiocytoma) dimples inward on lateral compression (Fitzpatrick sign) due to tethering to overlying epidermis. Histology shows spindle cells in storiform pattern with hemosiderin and foamy macrophages. IHC: Factor XIIIa positive.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with widespread erythroderma (>90% BSA involvement), pruritus, and exfoliation. CBC shows marked eosinophilia. Which of the following is NOT a common cause of erythroderma?
questions.exp: Common causes of erythroderma (L-POEM mnemonic): Lymphoma/leukaemia, Psoriasis, Others (PRP, seborrhoeic dermatitis), Eczema, Medications. Vitiligo is a hypopigmentary disorder and does not cause erythroderma.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male is being treated for multibacillary leprosy. He develops sudden onset of icterus, dark urine, and pallor 3 weeks after starting treatment. Which drug is responsible?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent haemolysis (especially in G6PD-deficient patients) and methaemoglobinaemia. Rifampicin causes hepatotoxicity and orange discolouration of body fluids. Clofazimine causes slate-grey skin pigmentation and GIT symptoms.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with a history of recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and hypopyon uveitis also develops pathergy. Which HLA type is strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease is characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis, and pathergy test positivity. It is strongly associated with HLA-B51, particularly in patients from the 'Silk Route' countries (Middle East, Asia). HLA-Cw6 is linked to psoriasis; HLA-B27 to spondyloarthropathies.

questions.q: A neonate presents at birth with congenital ichthyosis — generalized erythema with large plate-like scales. Skin biopsy shows absent or markedly reduced cornified envelope. Mutations in which gene are responsible for lamellar ichthyosis?
questions.exp: Lamellar ichthyosis (autosomal recessive) is most commonly caused by mutations in TGM1 (transglutaminase 1), which is essential for cornified cell envelope formation. KRT1/KRT10 mutations cause epidermolytic ichthyosis. FLG mutations cause ichthyosis vulgaris and predispose to atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old female with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis develops calcinosis cutis, Raynaud's phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasias. Which antibody is most specific for this subset?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis) is associated with anti-centromere antibody (ACA) in 70-80% of cases. Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc with ILD. Anti-RNA Pol III is associated with diffuse SSc and renal crisis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on the right thorax in a dermatomal distribution preceded by severe burning pain for 3 days. What is the most serious complication of this condition?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster: post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is the most common serious complication, defined as pain persisting >3 months after rash healing. It increases with age (>50 years) and immunosuppression. Treatment: tricyclic antidepressants, gabapentin, pregabalin, topical lidocaine patch.

questions.q: A 14-year-old presents with multiple flesh-coloured papules with central dell (umbilication) on the face and trunk. He is immunocompetent. Which virus is responsible?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by the poxvirus MCV (types 1-4). Characterised by umbilicated papules with a cheesy core (Henderson-Paterson bodies on histology). Self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals; extensive lesions suggest immunosuppression.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a recurrent BCC on the nose. What is the key principle of Mohs surgery?
opts: Excision with 5 mm clinical margin and standard vertical sections
Complete circumferential and deep margin examination using horizontal frozen sections
Punch biopsy followed by curettage and electrodessication
Wide local excision under general anaesthesia
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery achieves the highest cure rates for BCC/SCC by examining 100% of margins using horizontal (en face) frozen sections, allowing precise mapping and re-excision only of involved margins — maximising tissue conservation at cosmetically sensitive sites.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with ulceration and scarring of nasal septum, palate, and oropharynx. He is from a rural area. Serology is negative for syphilis and VDRL. Biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation. Leishman-Donovan bodies seen on smear. Diagnosis?
questions.exp: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (espundia, caused by L. braziliensis) causes destructive ulceration of nasal septum, palate, and pharynx. LD bodies (amastigotes) seen on smear/biopsy. Treatment: meglumine antimoniate or amphotericin B.

questions.q: A 30-year-old female presents with symmetrical hyperpigmentation on the cheeks, forehead, and upper lip that worsens with sun exposure. She is on oral contraceptives. Which layer of skin is predominantly affected when Wood's lamp accentuates the pigmentation?
questions.exp: Melasma (chloasma): Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal (superficial) pigment but not dermal pigment. Epidermal type responds better to topical depigmenting agents. Mixed type is most common. Treatment: triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + steroid), sunscreen.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male on methotrexate for psoriasis presents with nausea, oral ulcers, and pancytopenia. Which supplement prevents methotrexate-induced toxicity?
questions.exp: Folic acid 1-5 mg/day (on non-methotrexate days) prevents methotrexate-induced mucosal toxicity, GIT side effects, and haematological toxicity without significantly reducing efficacy. Folinic acid (leucovorin) is used as rescue therapy for acute toxicity/overdose.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with recurrent painless blistering on hands and feet following minor trauma since infancy. Nails are dystrophic. Biopsy under EM shows cleavage within the lamina lucida. Absence of which protein is responsible?
questions.exp: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (JEB) shows cleavage within the lamina lucida on EM. Herlitz (lethal) JEB is caused by mutations in LAMA3, LAMB3, or LAMC2 genes encoding laminin-332. Dystrophic EB has cleavage below lamina densa with absent type VII collagen.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with a warty plaque on the lower lip with induration and regional lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearls invading the dermis. The most important prognostic factor is:
questions.exp: In cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), site is a key prognostic factor. Lip SCC has a higher risk of nodal metastasis (10-15%) compared to SCC at other sun-exposed sites. Other high-risk sites include ear, temple, scalp, and non-sun-exposed areas. Breslow thickness is used for melanoma staging.
